extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting preprints to JMIR Preprints (JMIR and non-JMIR authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on how to post manuscripts to the JMIR Preprints server (both via journal opt-in and direct submission), how to solicit/nominate reviewers, required materials, and how preprint→partner-journal transfer works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission pathway options
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two pathways for manuscripts to appear here: 1) a submission to a JMIR or partner journal, where the author has checked the "open peer-review" checkbox, 2) Direct submissions to the preprint server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pathway 1: manuscript submitted to JMIR/partner journal with opt-in to preprinting. Pathway 2: direct submission to JMIR Preprints (no editor assigning reviewers). Choose pathway according to whether you want the preprint automatically considered during journal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer nomination and conflict-of-interest requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For direct submissions, authors are encouraged to nominate as many reviewers as possible; nominated peer-reviewers should be arms-length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominated reviewers should have no conflicts (be arms-length). Because there is no editor assigning reviewers for direct submissions, thorough and conflict-free nominations help secure community reviews and potential transfer to partner journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer-review setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are advised to set the setting to "open peer-review".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open peer-review enables community review on the preprint server and supports the 'manuscript marketplace' model where participating journals may use received reviews for transfer and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript format and abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts can be in any format. However, an abstract is required in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While file formatting is flexible for preprints, include a complete abstract to meet the server's requirements and to enable discoverability and reviewer assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: References formatting to enable automatic reviewer assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: We highly recommend to have the references in JMIR format (include a PMID) as then our system will automatically assign reviewers based on the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing references in JMIR style and including PMIDs improves the platform's ability to automatically identify and assign potential reviewers from the literature cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for transfer to partner journals
rubrics_metrics.description: For pathway 2, once a sufficient number of reviews has been received (and they are reasonably positive), the manuscript and peer-review reports may be transferred to a partner journal, whose editor may offer formal publication if the peer-review reports are addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer is conditional on receiving enough reviews of acceptable tone/content; transfer can result in a partner journal waiving its submission fee and potentially avoiding re-review if reports are addressed. Authors will be notified when the manuscript has enough reviewers and can choose whether to pursue transfer/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter instructions for journal consideration preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors do not wish to have the preprint considered in a partner journal (or a specific journal), this should be noted in the cover letter. Also, note if you want to have the paper only considered/forwarded to specific journals (e.g. JMIR, PLOS, PEERJ, BMJ Open, Nature Communications etc), please specify this in the cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cover letter to express opt-outs or explicit forwarding preferences to control which partner journals (if any) may receive your manuscript and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: No editor assignment for direct submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For pathway 2 (direct submissions), there is no editor assigning peer-reviewers, so authors must take steps to solicit reviews themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the platform will not assign reviewers for direct submissions, authors should nominate reviewers, promote the preprint, and ensure transparency/COI compliance to attract community reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-driven promotion to solicit reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: It will also help to tweet about your submission or posting it on your homepage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to actively publicize their preprint (social media, personal webpages) to increase visibility and likelihood of obtaining community reviews, which can enable transfer to partner journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer-review period per article
rubrics_metrics.description: Each preprint shows an 'Open Peer Review Period' with start and end dates (e.g., "Open Peer Review Period: May 9, 2026 - Jul 9, 2026").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints are displayed with a defined open peer-review window during which community reviews are solicited; authors and readers should note these dates for review opportunities and transfer timing.
